checks.item: Coverage: newly covered classes really describe symptoms
checks.evidence: Read the indexed pages cited (knowledge/index-t65/chunks.jsonl, joined per source/page). Cherry powdery mildew 201 (WSU: light green circular spot, white powdery coating underside, blistered leaves, depressed fruit areas) and 204 (UC IPM Cherry: white weblike growth on leaves/shoots/fruit, manifest crop cherry). Grape leaf blight: winegrapes8.pdf p12 section 'Leaf Blight, Isariopsis Leaf Spot' (large irregular dull red-brown spots turning black and brittle). TYLCV: 105 and 212 (upward curl, crumpling, interveinal yellowing, bushy). Tomato mosaic virus: 107, 218 (TMV/ToMV mottling, curl, stunting), 109. Orange HLB: CitrusOrange-Greening-Guide.pdf p1-2, OrangeFarming.pdf p4 (blotchy asymmetrical mottle, yellow shoots, dieback). Peach bacterial spot: BacterialSpotPeach.pdf p1 (water-soaked leaf spots turning purple, necrotic, shot holes). Squash powdery mildew: 143 (white powdery spots, leaf covered), 142, 267 (cucurbit powdery mildew; squash named in pages). Every cited (doc,page) exists in the index; quotes match. No false row found among the 26 yes rows I spot-read.

12 n/a rows are exactly the 12 *___healthy classes (apple, blueberry, cherry, corn, grape, peach, pepper, potato, raspberry, soybean, strawberry, tomato). 26 yes + 12 n/a = 38 = classes in datasets/manifests/lab.csv (test_every_class_has_a_coverage_row passes).

failures: datasets/rag/questions.jsonl test split: 'How do I control powdery mildew on my zucchini?' (not_in_documents, expected abstain) is now answerable from the new squash/cucurbit powdery mildew documents (141-146, 267). Reproduce: PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from sprout.rag.retrieve import Retriever; r=Retriever('<local path>'); print([(p.source,p.score) for p in r.search('How do I control powdery mildew on my zucchini?', crop='squash', k=3)])" -> 146-pddc-wisc-edu.html 0.914, 143-...powdery-mildew 0.735. The task required the questions' labels to keep holding; tests only check gold-page questions, and neither DECISIONS.md nor document-sources.md mentions that the corpus change invalidated this label. Needed: a recorded decision on how to handle it (it is a test-split question, so a replacement or exclusion has to be written down), plus a check in tests that no abstain question is answered by the corpus.

knowledge/manifest.csv: 18 of the 28 original rows have a blank source_url and 2 (strawberry.pdf, tomatodoc1.md) have no publisher, while the plan says each document keeps URL, publisher, title and date and docs/document-sources.md says the manifest holds them. tests/test_more_documents.py only checks files matching ^\d{3}-, so this passes unchecked. The coverage CSV cites tomatodoc2.md (no URL) as the only evidence for Tomato___Bacterial_spot and Tomato___Spider_mites. Either fill them in from the documents' own text or state in document-sources.md that these 28 predate the rule and have no recoverable URL.
notes: Coverage itself is sound: no false rows found among the 26 yes rows I read, and no class is uncovered. Index and GPU vectors check out. For T6.4: (1) use knowledge/index-t65 (not index) and it holds 5282 chunks, vectors cache name keyed to chunk text so Retriever loads it without re-embedding; (2) the zucchini abstain question above must be resolved before measuring abstention on rag_test; (3) each HTML page is one 'page 1' (up to ~15k chars) so page-level gold matching is coarse for new docs, and tomatodoc2.md is one 177k-char page; (4) some HTML docs keep nav lists (241, 203, 239); (5) crop is single-valued, so mixed tomato/pepper pages sit under one crop and crop-filtered retrieval for pepper can miss them (the decision entry admits this was not measured); (6) blueberry mummy berry query returned general blueberry pages only. The branch was cut before build commit e9ef258, so tests/test_container.py shows the old SPROUT_SECRET_KEY='x' in the diff; confirm the merge keeps the 32-char key.
